items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Louie, who else were the musicians around that time that you played with? All of them. Kid Ory, Bunk Johnson.

ctx.x: Louis, who would you say was the greatest influence on your life? Not in your youth, not musicians, I mean individuals. In your family or?

Well, my mother, she taught us the real things. She always said, you probably never get rich. She was wrong there, wasn't she? Well, she might be. Maybe, you know, maybe $10 million to save $10, you know. But I mean, what she means were have yachts and still got a zillion. We wasn't even thinking about that. She wasn't even thinking about it when she told me, say, but you'll always have health. So take a laxative every night of your life. And that's the finest things you ever told me. You didn't have much money…
When did you leave New Orleans?

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Fox Foster is mentioned by the interviewer, but the interviewee does not respond with any personal connection or relationship to him.

ctx.x: Kid O'Reilly. Oh, of course. He's still. Fox Foster.

You know what I mean? Well, what about, well, L. Hines is a young one. Yeah. But there ain't a very many that's from that New Orleans guy. No, that's why I'm not. Because most of them are still in New Orleans. They don't want to leave home. And after they come up and stay a while, they get home sick. Well, you know, that's no good.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] When you were talking earlier about your playing with Oliver and Kidore...

ctx.x: Well, I stayed with Oliver a long time. See what I mean? After I stayed with Oliver, we got so wedged in together making duets and musicians like Bix and Paul Whiteburn and all them people sitting down. They couldn't understand how we played so well together. When Joe got ready for a break, I had every note to it. And we just sitting right there and didn't say nothing to each other. That's how well I loved them. When did you start recording? When was the first? With Joe Oliver. About 1922. The same time of the…
When you were talking earlier about your playing with Oliver and Kidore, is there somebody now that's playing with you that you expect in the years to come will move to the forefront?

Well, every musician I have in my band because we don't have but one trumpet. So that means me. Yeah. I expect to do it. You're going to be doing all the movement. Well, that's what I mean. What about other orchestras around here? The mojo. I just got to relax. I know what it is. Just keep my stomach clean out.
